_about: Undecided holdouts ranked by closeness to a decision; written by holdouts/rank.py (see RANKING.md). score: judgement from recorded facts, not a probability.

outside.label: Outside proof to compile
outside.meaning: A complete outside proof exists; only checking it is left.

reported.label: Halt reported elsewhere
reported.meaning: Another group reports the halting step; a checked proof of it is left.

gap.label: One named gap
gap.meaning: A Lean reduction covers every case but one or two named ones.

finite.label: Finite or inequality question
finite.meaning: The macro model is proved; what is left is one invariant or inequality with no number theory in sight.

hunt.label: Halt hunt
hunt.meaning: An exact macro simulator exists and halting looks plausible; a long run could find the halt.

model.label: Model partly proved
model.meaning: Part of the macro structure is proved; the rule that decides halting is not.

number.label: Collatz-type question
number.meaning: Halting is reduced to an orbit of an explicit map that behaves like a Collatz problem.

decode.label: Not decoded yet
decode.meaning: The behaviour is described but its rules are not decoded.

cryptid.label: Cryptid
cryptid.meaning: A community cryptid: an open number-theory problem.

attacks.title: Finish compiling busycoq PR 60
attacks.what: Two complete Rocq halting proofs (credited to Yeyito on the bbchallenge wiki). The framework files compile and sample jobs pass; what is left is about 555 core-hours of native_compute jobs, now running in shards. A finished run moves both machines to decided.
attacks.need: Core-hours (a large machine would finish it in days).

attacks.title: Prove the reported vampire-family halts
attacks.what: Seven machines on four orbits. Lean already proves each halts iff its orbit of an explicit map reaches a halting context, and Thomas Reus's repository reports the halts at Bell 7.3·10^11 to 2.0·10^12. Left: list the contexts up to the halt (one long orbit.c run per orbit), and a chunked 2-adic check written in Lean with a soundness proof, evaluated by native_decide.
attacks.need: One large-memory machine for the orbit runs (the numbers reach 7·10^11 bits) and the Lean evaluation.

attacks.title: Close the Pascal machines' last two cases
attacks.what: Lean proves a bounce is a row of Pascal's triangle mod 2 and covers every right turn except an even head block meeting a walled zone and the crossing phase. Closing those makes the observed 2-cell-letter invariant a theorem: the two same-start machines never halt, the two mirrored starts follow by porting, and the slowed-down twin needs one more no-break argument.

attacks.title: Stack invariant for the wall-stack machine
attacks.what: Ranked first of the 40 map-reduced machines because no number theory is needed: the stack rules are in Lean, and an invariant that keeps each counter far above the one below would finish it.

attacks.title: Rule 102 machine: no danger pattern
attacks.what: The round trip, the jump and its clock are in Lean, and so is which gaps can reach the danger pattern: under shielded sweeps the rows of Pascal's triangle mod 2, at the next jump one rest per jump length (mask L). Left: control the words that enter the gap at the wall between jumps, and show no new bulk 10 is born.

attacks.title: Automaton search on the clock-and-word maps (R02)
attacks.what: The clock lemma is in Lean for six tables. Left is one finite-state question per machine: a regular language of words that the word map P keeps and that never triggers the halting rebuild. A SAT search on the word alone is far smaller than the whole-tape search that failed.
attacks.need: Solver time (many CPU-hours of SAT, easy to parallelise).

attacks.title: Rebuild maps and the wall invariant (R07)
attacks.what: Up/down counters and two binary counters with rebuilds. The rebuilds are explicit closed maps (checked, not proved); prove them in Lean and extend the PR 57/58 wall invariant to rebuilds that read only part of the counter. What remains after that is a number-theoretic inequality.

attacks.title: Binary counters with doublers: defects die out
attacks.what: A tape with one travelling defect cannot halt. Prove that every defect disappears before the next round (one inequality on irregular digits) and the pair is non-halting.

attacks.title: Halt hunts on the countdown counters (R04, R11)
attacks.what: Base-4 and ternary odometers with countdown timers. Short-timer tapes of this shape are proved to halt, and this kind of family gave half the decisions of the week of 13 November. Exact odometer jumps (the PR 83 / 89 method) to the first top-level overflow; the collapse pair has an exact cycle law already.
attacks.need: Long CPU runs, one machine each.

attacks.title: Front speed of the cascade for the four R08 machines
attacks.what: The leftmost-zone reduction and the two-zone cascade are proved in Lean; halting is one explicit cascade of one-bit cells. A bound on the speed of the front (measured: 3.3 cells per doubling) would give huge no-halt bounds; deciding needs a new idea about the old zone once the front reaches it.

machines.famname: Clock and word: a block grows in doubling time while a word map runs 2^k times
machines.why: A clock at the right end: at each visit the block 1^(1+4k) has grown by 4 and the word beside it has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one trip of the head) — proved in Lean for every k whenever the 2^k trips all return, on the mirror image of the machine. machines.famname: Collatz-like maps and cryptids (parked)
machines.why: An odometer that is exactly a doubling map: u ↦ 2u modulo v, v growing by one each operation, the left block counting the wrap-arounds allowed before a reset. Proved in Lean (kernel): it halts iff a reset happens with 2u = v. No halt in 10^11 operations (54 resets); heuristically about 10^-10 for a later halt; open. Accelerated run: no halt in 1.89e22 steps.
machines.next: None: pure number theory (resets are logarithmically rare: reset k needs ~1.47^k operations).

machines.name: probviously halting
machines.why: Hydra-like: each epoch eats a run of c ones 4 at a time while a block grows by X -> floor(3X/2)+5; c mod 4 and the last parity decide halt or a new, vastly longer epoch. Proved in Lean: halts iff this iteration reaches its halting case; epochs 0-3 computed, epoch 4 (c with ~2*10^13 digits) is out of reach and would halt at its end with heuristic chance 3/4. Accelerated run: no halt in 2.61e49522 steps.
machines.next: None feasible: the epoch-4 end needs parities after 1.1x10^14 steps of X -> floor(3X/2)+5 on ~10^13-digit numbers (~10^27 bit operations).

Each round turns one q of the first q-block into a p and adds a p to the first p-block (proved in Lean); when the first q-block is used up an epoch ends, and a new, larger first block is built from the whole stack; the sizes follow a Collatz-like rule. Accelerated run: no halt in 3.54e36 steps.
machines.next: Extract the epoch-end rule (how the new top block is built from the stack) and prove it with symtm.
